title: Labs
summary: A growing playground of small interactive demos I build to learn things in public.
body:
Labs is where I prototype the stuff I want to actually understand. Each demo is its own little page, focused on one idea, shipped fast and refined later. Some of them show up in the demos section of this site as embeds, others just live in the labs index.

It's plain HTML and TypeScript, built with Vite and hosted on GitHub Pages. No framework, no app shell, just one page per idea. That constraint is the point. It keeps each demo legible end to end, and it means I can fork one, change one variable, and learn something without fighting the tooling.

If a demo gets enough legs to feel like a real project, it graduates out of labs into its own thing. Most won't, and that's fine. Labs is the workshop, not the showroom.

title: This site
summary: Working-in-public portfolio in Vue 3 + Tailwind 4. Built as its own design playground.
body:
This is my site, I built it because I wanted somewhere public to put the work I actually do. Projects, demos, notes, that kind of thing. The typical resume portfolio template never really fit the way I think about what I'm building, so I just made my own.

It's Vue 3 with Tailwind 4, using the new `@theme` directive so there's no Tailwind config file to maintain. Vite handles the build, and I leaned on `vite.config.ts` a bit more than the default. There's a small plugin in there that serves the RSS feed in dev so I don't have to rebuild to test it, `vite-imagetools` runs at build time to spit out AVIF, WebP, and JPEG variants of every hero image across a few widths, and a tiny shim keeps those picture imports working under Vitest. List content lives in typed JSON files under `src/content/`, and the singleton stuff like about, education, work history, and the home status box sits in `src/data/`. Detail pages render markdown through marked, and code blocks get highlighted by Shiki with a dual light and dark theme that follows the site's own theme switch.

The comic theme isn't just for looks either. Every panel sits at a slight angle, every hover lifts it up like you're peeling back to "the next page" underneath. There's a loader pulse that crossfades into the actual content on each page so you don't see things popping in. Skip to content is wired for keyboard users, reduced motion gets respected, and there's a Vitest suite covering components, pages, composables, and utils so I can keep moving without breaking things. It's a work in progress by design, the site is the playground, I'm figuring out the design as I go.
